en.title: Netflix's 'Sacrifice': A Star-Studded Volcano Thriller You Might Skip
en.summary: Anya Taylor-Joy and Chris Evans star in a new Netflix film where a terrorist group threatens a volcanic sacrifice. Early reviews suggest this ambitious project might not stick the landing.
en.body:
The autumn release calendar is often a deluge of big books, but this year, Netflix is adding a cinematic spectacle to the mix. **Sacrifice**, directed by **Romain Gavras**, lands with a premise that’s as dramatic as it is potentially baffling: a terrorist group demanding a prophecy be fulfilled by sacrificing three chosen individuals into a volcano. Starring **Anya Taylor-Joy** and **Chris Evans**, the film promises a visually ambitious, albeit contentious, viewing experience.

The film's plot centers on this extreme ultimatum, an 'eat-the-rich' satire wrapped in a thriller. However, early critical reception suggests that while the film boasts impressive production values and a stellar cast including **Vincent Cassel**, **Salma Hayek Pinault**, and **John Malkovich**, its narrative coherence and thematic depth are questionable. Some reviews point to a "tonal incompetence" and "incoherent amalgamation of themes," indicating that the spectacle might not be enough to carry the story.

## The Volcano's Verdict: Stream It or Skip It?

When a film features prominent stars like **Chris Evans** and **Anya Taylor-Joy** in a high-stakes scenario, anticipation is naturally high. Yet, the buzz surrounding **Sacrifice** is decidedly mixed. Critics are grappling with its provocative themes and the execution of its central conflict. The film seems to aim for a profound statement on societal issues, but the narrative struggles to tie its ambitious ideas together cohesively. This leaves potential viewers in a familiar predicament: is the visual flair and the star power enough to warrant the watch, or will it be a case of style over substance?

## What the Critics Are Saying

While specific fan reactions are still emerging, the critical consensus offers a glimpse into the film's reception. Some critics have lauded the film's visual grandeur and its daring attempt at social commentary. However, a significant portion of reviews highlight significant flaws in the storytelling and thematic clarity. As one review noted, the film feels like "the sort of disaster that even Netflix would shy away from releasing," primarily due to its narrative shortcomings. This suggests that while **Sacrifice** might spark conversation, it may not be the universally acclaimed hit some were hoping for.

## What's Next

For those intrigued by the concept or the cast, **Sacrifice** is now available to stream on Netflix. Whether it becomes a cult favorite or a cautionary tale in ambitious filmmaking remains to be seen. Meanwhile, the literary world continues its own fall onslaught with major releases from authors like **Elizabeth Hand**, **Becky Chambers**, **M. John Harrison**, **Lynn D. Jung**, and **Claire North**, offering a wealth of reading material for those seeking narrative depth.

content_raw: News What to Watch What to Watch and Read This Weekend: I Don’t Know What to Do With the Netflix Volcano Sacrifice Movie Plus: All the books, all at once and an excuse to finally watch Save Yourselves! By Molly Templeton | Published on October 16, 2026 Photo Credit: Netflix Comment 1 Share New Share Photo Credit: Netflix Welcome to another week of All the Books! The fall continues to be the fall, which is to say, the season in which publishing believes it needs to release all the “big” books. I won’t bore you with a tirade on this topic; I will just say that we all only have so much time to read, and may have to be quite selective, perhaps tactical, about how to balance our reading time with the rest of the million things tugging at our attention at any given moment. But there are also movies! Next week is my own personal Barbenheimer—Wickerwood?—but while one waits for that, one could watch Anya Taylor-Joy try to throw Chris Evans into a volcano. If one wanted. There’s a lot, honestly. Grab a warm beverage, pet a cat (or dog, I guess), call your reps, hug your friends, and watch some leaves fall. Then there’s so much to read. I Hope You Have a Lot of Time for Reading This Fall You may (or may not) remember that about a month ago, I was marveling about how many books came out on the same weekend. Well, October said “hold my beer.” Someone somewhere seems to have decided that the second week of the month is when we get a huge number of big SFF books, and so this week we get (deep breath!): Elizabeth Hand’s Unspeakable Things ! Becky Chambers’ new novel As You Wake, Break the Shell ! M. John Harrison’s Booker Prize-shortlisted The End of Everything ! Lynn D. Jung’s Mothsblood ! And Claire North’s As We Fall Through Time ! To name just a few! I don’t really know what to do with myself here. What are we reading first? I Also Don’t Know What to Do With the Netflix Volcano Sacrifice Movie So, when I first heard about Sacrifice , I thought it sounded delightful. Possibly amazing. “A high-end charity gala is raided by a violent group of radicals on a mystical quest to fulfill a prophecy” is what we were told . Now, though, I don’t know what to think. The trailer is somehow … not weird enough. Why does this movie seem so normal , even as Anya Taylor-Joy seeks to pitch Chris Evans into a volcano? What is not quite right here? The movie does have Vincent Cassel, eternal weirdo. But the presence of Taylor-Joy means I can’t help but think of The Menu , which was also not quite weird enough. And yet. I want it to be good. I am trying to retain a little bit of optimism here. I’m trying .
